thesis: A scheduler is useful when it routes accepted triggers, bids, solver results, proof jobs, and settlement reviews without pretending to be protocol-level automation.

runThisFirst.title: Replay the accepted scheduler trigger
runThisFirst.userGoal: See a scheduler intent become an executed app job without trusting a hidden backend.
steps: Check the accepted intent receipt and accepted execution receipt.
Confirm the winning bid and blocked stale/slow bids.
Treat the row as app-state only after accepted receipt, transfer match, and replay checks pass.
runThisFirst.expectedResult: The trigger remains executed, the local-key payout remains matched, and stale or duplicate candidates stay blocked.
runThisFirst.nextUpgrade: Replace local-key execution with external-wallet signing, then replay the accepted txid before promotion.

jobs.title: Accepted trigger -> execution
jobs.expected: Pool net must satisfy poolNetTkas >= 60 before execution.
jobs.observed: 4 TKAS execution transfer matched accepted receipt.

jobs.title: Executor bid selection
jobs.expected: Pick the lowest valid bid that satisfies latency and source policy.
jobs.observed: local-pool-operator selected; stale or too-slow bids remain blocked.

jobs.title: Scheduler intent -> covenant proof binding
jobs.expected: A scheduler row can reference an accepted covenant proof without upgrading itself into protocol scheduling.
blockedCases: binding cannot promote without an accepted proof txid
binding entrypoint must match the referenced proof row
accepted binding payload does not upgrade indexer-derived scheduler state into protocol scheduling

jobs.title: Transparent coordination pack
jobs.expected: Signed compatible intendos should form a pack only when threshold conditions are satisfied.
blockedCases: coordinated atomic execution across independent participants

jobs.title: Auction settlement review
jobs.expected: Winner release and loser refund rows need accepted planner evidence, amount-matched custody, wallet review, and accepted replay.
jobs.observed: 2 custody rows ready; 3 settlement rows reviewed.

jobs.title: Agent task release / hold / refund
jobs.expected: Release, hold, or refund can be scheduled only after task/proof/dispute evidence and wallet-reviewed settlement agree.
blockedCases: Settlement review needs custody source, reviewer decision, wallet standard, and accepted replay.
Dispute holds stay held until reviewed.

expectedBehavior: Accepted trigger receipts can make an app job eligible.
Execution is promoted only when the accepted execution receipt and accepted transfer evidence match.
Executor bids can be ranked by explicit policy, but winner selection stays planner/indexer state until settlement is wallet-reviewed and accepted.
Coordination packs can be solved transparently now; private accumulation and atomic Hunt execution remain research.
Auction and agent settlement rows stay blocked until custody source, wallet-standard signing, submit result, and accepted replay all match.
predictionsToTestNext: A duplicate scheduler execution receipt should stay blocked.
A low-fee but too-slow scheduler bid should lose to a valid faster bid.
A stale-source bid should never win even if its price is attractive.
A satisfiable coordination pack should produce exactly one selected settlement route.
A disputed agent task should stay held until reviewer decision and wallet review are attached.
boundaries: This is a TN12 app workbench, not a protocol universal scheduler.
It schedules reviewable jobs over accepted evidence; it does not create autonomous custody.
The full research target still needs privacy, capital multiplexing, solver incentives, censorship resistance, MEV resistance, and atomic execution.
